open_points.subject: agent-authority checks
open_points.text: The decision says “every agent-authority call is checked three times”, but rule 1 says “‘Register an agent session’ is checked for the token only”, while session operations without a project are checked only for the token and registered session.
open_points.question: Are checks operation-dependent—one for registration, two for session-only operations and three for project operations—or must every agent-authority call undergo three checks?
options: Use one, two or three checks according to the operation
Define meaningful session and project checks for every call
open_points.default_guess: Use the qualified normative rule: one check for registration, two for session-only operations and three for project operations.

open_points.subject: confirmation expiry
open_points.text: A confirmation value “is valid only in that session, for 10 minutes”, while the test only says one “older than 10 minutes is refused”.
open_points.question: Is a confirmation submitted exactly 10 minutes after it was shown valid or expired?
options: Expire when now is greater than or equal to shown instant plus 10 minutes
Expire only when now is greater than shown instant plus 10 minutes

open_points.subject: archiving an anonymised project
open_points.text: Rule 1 says archiving a project states its revision; rule 3 says “An anonymised project ... [has] no revision” and “an action on them states none”; A05 also says archiving an already archived project is an accepted no-op, and an anonymised project has status `archived`.
open_points.question: What happens when the owner submits archive for an anonymised project, and must that submission state a revision?
options: Accept it unchanged without a revision
Refuse it because the project is anonymised
Require a revision even though none exists
open_points.default_guess: Accept it unchanged without a revision.

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and the confirmation is bound to that digest, but no digest algorithm or exact bytes to digest are declared.
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and byte representation identify and bind an uploaded import file?
options: SHA-256 of the exact uploaded bytes
A release-declared digest algorithm and canonicalised file representation
A backend-selected digest
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 of the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: pre-import backup deletion
open_points.text: Rule 10 says that after a checked backup holding the closure, “Registry deletes every backup made before the import, so no kept backup can bring back a store without the closure”; M10 says “no backup without it is kept”. A18, however, allows a backup deletion to fail and be retried later while Registry keeps serving.
open_points.question: If deletion of a pre-import backup fails after the closure backup passes, may that old backup remain until a later run, or must Registry stop serving or otherwise ensure it is no longer kept?
options: Allow it to remain and retry, weakening the categorical M10 statement
Do not resume normal service until all pre-import backups are removed
Quarantine the failed target so it is no longer a restorable kept backup
open_points.default_guess: Quarantine it from restoration and retry physical deletion later.

open_points.subject: new-store startup condition
open_points.text: “An empty store location is made into a new, empty store”, but “empty store location” is not defined.
open_points.question: Which filesystem states count as an empty store location: a missing path, an empty directory, a zero-length file, or some subset of these?
options: Only a missing path
A missing path or empty directory
A missing path, empty directory or zero-length file
open_points.default_guess: Treat only a missing path or an empty directory as new; refuse a zero-length or otherwise malformed store file.

open_points.subject: backup with no audit entries
open_points.text: Every backup records “the last audit sequence number it holds”, and its check verifies that “its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”, but a new store can have no audit entry.
open_points.question: What value is recorded and what check is performed when the backed-up audit log is empty?
options: Record `null` and require an empty audit log
Record `0` and treat it as the pre-entry sequence
Omit the field for an empty log
open_points.default_guess: Record `0` and require that the audit log contain no entries.

open_points.subject: backup encryption format
open_points.text: A backup is “encrypted with the backup key” and records “a digest of the key”, but the cipher, authentication mode, nonce handling, treatment of keys longer than 32 bytes, key-digest algorithm and backup container format are not fixed.
open_points.question: What authenticated-encryption and key-handling rules must every backend use for backups?
options: Fix an authenticated scheme, nonce rules, KDF and key-digest algorithm in State 2
Let each backend choose while satisfying confidentiality and integrity checks
Defer the complete encrypted backup format to State 6
open_points.default_guess: Fix an authenticated format using AES-256-GCM with a random nonce, derive a 256-bit key with HKDF-SHA-256, and identify the configured key with SHA-256.

open_points.subject: restore recovery-point bound
open_points.text: Rule 7 says “a restore loses at most a day of changes” while rule 9 permits the owner to restore “a backup”; kept backups may be up to 30 days old.
open_points.question: Must production always be restored from the newest checked backup for the one-day loss bound to hold, or may the owner deliberately restore an older kept backup?
options: Require the newest checked backup
Permit any checked backup and qualify the one-day bound as applying only to the newest
Permit an older backup only through an explicit exceptional procedure
open_points.default_guess: Permit any checked backup, but state that the one-day recovery-point bound applies only when restoring the newest checked backup.

open_points.subject: post-restore reconciliation
open_points.text: The owner must reconcile retained, erased, restricted and ended states “before configuring the tokens and starting it again”, but Registry “cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done”.
open_points.question: What prevents service tokens from being enabled before the required post-restore reconciliation is complete, and what evidence marks completion?
options: Nothing technical; this is solely an owner procedure
A durable reconciliation-complete marker gates token-enabled startup
A separately verified release or configuration flag authorises token-enabled startup
open_points.default_guess: Add a durable reconciliation-complete marker that is required before a token-enabled start.

open_points.subject: backend lowering of caller values
open_points.text: The rule requires that a caller value “never becomes an identifier, an operator or syntax”, but then says “How the store's backend lowers this is the backend's” and gives no backend-independent acceptance test for that property.
open_points.question: What evidence or test establishes that a backend's lowering preserves the fixed command structure for every caller-controlled value and every operation?
options: Require native bound-value facilities wherever the backend supports values
Define backend-specific reviewed lowering rules and injection tests
Treat the semantic statement alone as sufficient without prescribing evidence
open_points.default_guess: Require backend-specific reviewed lowering rules, using native bound values where available, with adversarial tests for every operation.

open_points.subject: security review status after A19 change
open_points.text: A21 rule 2 says “A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.” The `injection_interpreted_input` category names A19, and A19 has changed, but A21 still says “Security review: PERFORMED” and that the review is complete.
open_points.question: Has the changed A19 been re-reviewed so A21 may remain performed, or is A21 now reopened pending a new injection review?
options: Record a new completed review of the changed A19
Mark A21 reopened until that review occurs
open_points.default_guess: Mark A21 reopened until the changed A19 is reviewed and the outcome is recorded.
